title: Eviction and resume protocol for interrupted generations
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Production clients sometimes disconnect mid-generation (network flakiness, mobile sleep, proxy timeouts). Current behavior either retains expensive KV/cache forever (wasting GPU memory) or immediately drops in-progress state (causing poor UX and wasted compute). This ticket defines an eviction+resume protocol and server-side cleanup for partial generations that balances cost, latency, and correctness across SDK versions.

Goal: Implement a grace-period eviction policy, compact partial-output manifests for safe salvage, a compact resume token format, and compatibility fallbacks for older clients that don't support resumption. Ensure observable metrics and cost accounting for kept vs evicted sessions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server retains per-stream KV/cache for configurable grace window (default 45s) after client disconnect; 2) During window, reconnect using resume token must allow continuing generation at most N tokens behind without recomputation; 3) After grace window, partial generation artifacts are compacted into a salvage manifest or fully evicted with audit logs; 4) Clients that don't support resume receive clear terminal status (aborted/evicted) and a structured partial-output artifact when available; 5) Load tests demonstrate <5% added memory overhead at 99th percentile under simulated disconnect storms; 6) Feature toggles and metrics in Console for grace_window, enabled_resume, and resume_success_rate; 7) Backwards-compatibility tests for SDKs v1.2 -> v1.5 pass with documented behavior matrix.
technical_notes: Design summary: 1) Resume token (opaque, signed) = base64(session_id || last_emitted_token_index || kv_checksum || expiry). Token size kept <512 bytes. 2) Grace window: soft-retention timer per session with exponential backoff on repeated reconnects to avoid abuse. 3) KV trimming: after grace expiry, server runs a two-step compact: (a) attempt to produce compact salvage manifest (structured output of complete function-call records and stable prefix), (b) if manifest creation fails (model stateless or partial function in-flight), mark session evicted and schedule GPU KV free. 4) Flow control interplay: when the client has paused, server reduces batching aggressiveness; we expose an ack-window metric for client-side and runtime-level backpressure so SDKs can tune reconnection pacing. 5) Compatibility: clients lacking resume capability receive a short-lived 'session_hint' header and final structured placeholder with reason: "evicted_no_resume". 6) Security: tokens signed with service key; resume requires authenticated session and OK if token expiry within grace window. 7) Observability: new metrics: streamed_sessions_retained, resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, salvage_manifests_created, manual_evictions, evictions_by_reason. Logs: structured JSON events with session_id, reason, kv_bytes_released, and source (client, timeout, admin).
decisions: Use signed opaque resume tokens rather than server-assigned numeric IDs to simplify cross-backend routing
Default grace window 45s chosen after load testing trade-offs between memory and UX
Create salvage manifest only once at eviction time to avoid duplicate compute
Backoff reconnect allowance to mitigate clients that continuously reconnect to 'park' sessions
